subject: Risky decision making models for gain only or loss only decisions

messages.author: 5605ce987fbf5469
messages.subject: Risky decision making models for gain only or loss only decisions
parts:
Hi and thanks for the great resource! I am interested in using the models for the decision-making tasks, particularly the risk aversion task (ra_noLA) the risk-aversion parameter and tau (inverse temperature). However, I noticed that the model requires a "loss" column in the data where the value of a loss option is specified. I'm interested in applying the model to cases where subjects choose between a safe win option and a risky win option, and a safe loss option and a risky win option, in other words, a design that doesn't involve any mixed loss and win gambles. I was wondering if it was still possible to use the package for these kinds of decisions, or if you might have suggestions about whether it would be straightforward to change the model code to capture these kind of decisions?

Thanks,
Jessica Mollick

Best,

messages.subject: Re: Risky decision making models for gain only or loss only decisions
parts:
Hi Young,
Thank you for the information. I took a look at the peer_OCU model and it is quite similar to the experiment design I'm thinking of. Basing off some of the inputs in the peer_OCU model, I have uploaded a sample file of three subjects' simulated data- as you can see, it is a quite similar design, where we have a different probability of payoff for each gamble, compared to a safe option. The main difference is that the safe option would not be probabilistic, but they would always receive it if they chose it. However, is there an option to turn off the other conferred utility if I was looking at solo decisions?

Explanation of the columns:
p_gamble: The probability of getting the risky_Hpayoff amount
safe: the value of the safe option- in this case, it is always given with 100% probability
risky_HPayoff: Highest possible payoff for risky option
risky_LPayoff: Lowest possible payoff for risky option: nothing
choice: simulated subject choices

The parameters I want to estimate from this set of decisions are the rho/risk aversion parameter and inverse temperature.

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: Risky decision making models for gain only or loss only decisions
parts:
Hi Jessica,

Thanks for the sample data. What's different in your data (compared to the data used in the ra_prospect or ra_noLA model) is that the probability of receiving a high outcome from a risky option is not always 50%. So you would need to change this line in the ra_noLA model:

evGamble = 0.5 * (pow(gain[i, t], rho[i]) - pow(loss[i, t], rho[i]));

You may also want to include a probability weighting function, but it's up to you. We plan to include a more general model including a probability weighting function in the future, but can't guarantee when it will be released. Hope this helps. 

Best,
Young

Jessica

evSafe     = - pow(cert[i,t], rho[i]);

SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'ra_noLA_edit_losses' NOW (CHAIN 1).

  Log probability evaluates to log(0), i.e. negative infinity.

library(hBayesDM)
output <- ra_noLA_edit_losses(data = "choose", niter = 2000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 3, ncore = 3)
plotInd(output, "rho")

Jessica

parts:
Hi Jessica,


Those messages pop up when the initial parameter values lead to some problem in evaluating the likelihood function (i.e. it evaluates to positive or negative infinity). That said, once the sampler tries reasonable values and begins sampling, you should be fine! 


Nate

From: hbayesd...@googlegroups.com <hbayesd...@googlegroups.com> on behalf of Jessica Mollick <jmol...@gmail.com>
Sent: Wednesday, October 17, 2018 3:49:42 PM
To: Woo-Young Ahn
Cc: hbayesdm-users
Subject: Re: Risky decision making models for gain only or loss only decisions

Hi Young,

Thank you! I think that changing the upper and lower bounds for the "cert" parameter fixed my problem, at least enough that I was able to estimate the model. Should I be concerned if I still get the warning message below, perhaps related to some other parameter? How would I figure out which one it is?

Rejecting initial value:
  Log probability evaluates to log(0), i.e. negative infinity.
  Stan can't start sampling from this initial value.

Here are the changes I made to allow cert to be a sure loss:
real<lower=-100,upper=100> cert[N,T]; 
evSafe   = -pow(cert[i,t], rho[i]);

The script with these changes is attached in case it's useful to others. Look forward to seeing the new model!

On Tue, Oct 16, 2018 at 1:40 AM, Woo-Young Ahn <wooyou...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Jessica,

I believe the message is related to initial values for hyper parameters. Check existing R codes how we assign initial values for parameters with specific upper and lower bounds. When we release the new model, we will take care of the issue. Thanks!

Best,
Young

I'd be very interested in any scripts you come up with for a loss-only version, and the more flexible version of the toolbox when it's released.

I tried putting a negative sign in front of the cert option in the stan script to capture a sure loss, but I don't think that it worked. 

evSafe     = - pow(cert[i,t], rho[i]); 

This is what happens when I try and run my modified "loss only" version:
SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'ra_noLA_edit_losses' NOW (CHAIN 1).
Rejecting initial value:
  Log probability evaluates to log(0), i.e. negative infinity.
  Stan can't start sampling from this initial value.

I've attached the scripts and text file I edited, in case they are helpful as you look into this further!

To run these in R, I just use the code snippet below:
library(hBayesDM)
output <- ra_noLA_edit_losses(data = "choose", niter = 2000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 3, ncore = 3)
plotInd(output, "rho")

Jessica

Hi Young,
Thank you for the pointer to the line to change in the ra_noLA model. However, I have another question to make sure I understand correctly - what should I put for the loss column? As in the csv I uploaded, if the risky gamble doesn't pay off, then subjects will get 0 dollars. It looks like the ra_noLA model needs a non-zero number in the loss column. If their gamble does not pay off, then participants will lose the value of the certain option, so I could try putting in the amount they would lose as a negative number in the loss column (-5 for example is what they lose if a 50% gamble for 5 dollars doesn't pay off)? On Wednesday, May 16, 2018 at 2:23:23 PM UTC-4, Woo-Young Ahn wrote:
Hi Jessica,

Thanks for the sample data. What's different in your data (compared to the data used in the ra_prospect or ra_noLA model) is that the probability of receiving a high outcome from a risky option is not always 50%. So you would need to change this line in the ra_noLA model:

evGamble = 0.5 * (pow(gain[i, t], rho[i]) - pow(loss[i, t], rho[i]));

You may also want to include a probability weighting function, but it's up to you. We plan to include a more general model including a probability weighting function in the future, but can't guarantee when it will be released. Hope this helps. 

Best,
Young
